newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen supported at lower levels into Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen supported at lower levels into Thursday.

text.p: Bund futures drifted at lower levels much of Wednesday after slightly stronger than expected third quarter German GDP and weak U.S. Treasuries sparked rounds of selling.
Traders said they expected the market to now drift sideways between 102.30 and 102.55 ahead of Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting and unemployment numbers which are due in the morning.
In late afternoon trade, the December DTB Bund future was down 27 basis points at 102.36, but well off an early low of 102.27 set shortly after the market opened.
Traders said a major theme of the day was the roll-over of the December futures contract to the March contract, but that the switch had little impact on prices.
They added that overall signs of slow German economic growth and a strong U.S. bond market should keep Bunds supported. "I do not see any big retreat before the end of the week," one trader said.
All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters said they expect the Bundesbank to keep rates on hold at its meeting Thursday and indeed for the rest of the year.
The stronger than expected third quarter GDP hurt Bunds in relation to Treasuries. The Bund/T-note spread narrowed two basis points and stood at 49 basis points late in the day.
The DTB March Bund future was down 28 basis points in late trade at 101.45.
